S-A (approved): an exercise first executed in the break’s week enters a moderate or long return at the entry, with its last executed whole count as the ceiling; E, O, B and ceiling disagreements at 0 in every class and length measured.

S-B (approved): after a short break a loaded exercise whose first log the break left unadopted is established by effort again (UNLOGGED, at most effortGuidedLoad.sets = 2, RIR 3 or more, at its executed repetitions); a bodyweight exercise set up before a short break continues at its normal count. S-C (approved as the declared reading): an exposure that missed its logged target is performed (in use) but gives no ceiling count; the ceiling falls back as declared (the earlier executed count, else the known count, else the normal count). Rises stay one set per executed whole week, gated on post-return targets (R36 records the met/missed asymmetry for the next policy revision).

S-D (approved): a re-establishment executed before a break is a fact: a moderate or long return takes the re-establishment count as the ceiling; after a short break the load is established by effort again (at most 2 sets, under the earlier load) and the count comes back one set per executed whole week (D53). R35 records the cost for the next policy revision.

S-E (approved): each short break owns its easy slot; a separate later short break takes the first quality slot still ahead that no break has eased (reading a: an eased run is no longer a quality slot), so when the first break’s slot is still ahead both run easy; a newer report of the same break keeps its slot; exactly one slot per break.

S-F (approved): a short break during the return steps resumes the step reached; a weekly review decided after the break began does not count, so the entry may repeat once (conservative); nothing returns to the dose before an earlier break. R7AB-SSCTR-r1: the step reached is the evidence-anchored one (WEEK_START_AUTHORITY_CONTRACT §3-§4); steps executed after the last evidence-anchored start are facts only, so on an unconsolidated re-entry week the entry may repeat after more than one executed week, and a strength-only shortfall also repeats the run entry (conservative; NF-R7AB-1, routed as R40). R7ASE-SSCTR-r1: the step reached is read value by value and per sport (STATE_EVIDENCE_CONTRACT §4): a strength shortfall no longer repeats an executed run step, nor the reverse (R40 applied), and a value a review carried from a projection is rebuilt on history by the review’s rule.
S-G (approved): the entry repetition target of an exercise first executed before the break is the one it was executed at.

R7AB S-A (approved): after an unfinished, unreviewed re-entry week, a later interruption starts from the re-entry plus the executed facts, whatever was decided meanwhile (equipment, fatigue, schedule, goal or event changes, a no-op statement); only the weekly review’s rule on the complete week, by a review or a handler applying it, may step what was executed in it, and the run holds when a run was missed.

R7AB S-B (approved, with NF-R7AB-1 routed as R40): completed sessions anchor a projected start only when the week executed exactly as the projection assumed, loads included; a lighter effort-guided load leaves the start to a review (which adopts it) or to the re-entry plus facts; a known load the athlete did not lift is never prescribed from a projection.

R7AB S-C (approved): a first interruption after an unconsolidated week moves back to the last evidence-anchored start; on a never-logged program this is the intake: runs from the intake capacity and return target, a known exercise at its reported load, an exercise never performed by the first-exposure establishment (D51, D52; effortGuidedLoad, at most 2 sets at RIR 3 or more), never a return step of a count or load the plan only assumed; with a known exercise in the return steps, exercises first set up in the entry week follow the entry (1 set, RIR 4 or more).
R7AB S-D (approved, with NF-R7AB-1): inside a return, a value a review held from a projected start is not history until a week is executed in full; a later short interruption resumes it at the entry.

R7AB S-E (approved as the Founder-decided ASK, §11): a named correction that puts its interruption on or after training executed after its own return began is asked when it changes a prescription; the plan in force stays the first return’s; no pre-break dose is restored.
R7AB S-F (approved): no unexecuted return step, load or whole count reaches a ceiling or a resumed dose through a stored start (D49, D53, D56).

R7ASE SE-A (approved): no prescription changes before a return: the R5 corpus, the profiles and the simulations are identical and the R6 holdout differs only in two returns after unreported weeks (H17, H26), with no status change; the planner is unchanged.

R7ASE SE-B (approved, with NF-R7ASE-1 routed as R41): a return starts from what the athlete executed, value by value, never from a value only a projection made (a load step, a load tick, a whole count or an easy week the plan assumed in a week not executed as assumed); after weeks never reported, the run value is the last evidence-anchored one and may sit below what reported weeks executed (conservative).

R7ASE SE-C (approved): in a week read as facts, a known load the athlete lifted on a known-load row is the exercise’s load: lighter, or heavier only under D44 (at most one smallest increment above the row, the row’s target met); a fact, never a step; an effort-guided row adopts nothing; history then equals what the weekly review would adopt.

R7ASE SE-D (approved with conditions, NF-R7ASE-3 routed as R42): a projected dose the athlete then lifted exactly is history for its load and for its repetitions as the target that goes with that load; with repetitions unlogged the load lifted is still the fact, the repetitions stay the target and no step is taken; a tick counted at a lower load is never carried onto the projected one. Not approved as history: a stored load tick at the lifted load that counts an exposure the projection assumed and the athlete did not execute; until R42, its sporting reach is bounded to the unchanged planner’s own no-break progression (one load step one successful exposure earlier, under the ceiling in a moderate or long return).

R7ASE SE-E (approved; R40 applied): per sport, a sport executed exactly as its projection assumed keeps its completed sessions when the other sport did not; never a step the sport did not execute; strength and run each equal or trail the reviewed control.

R7ASE SE-F (approved): a value a weekly review’s start carried from a projection is rebuilt by the review’s own rule on the historical value (never trusted whole, never walked back whole); a Sunday handler that applies the review’s rule is that sport’s review (E6), a Monday handler changes no history. SE-E and SE-F supersede the whole-start reading of R7AB S-B and S-D where they differ.
R7ASE SE-G (approved): a last performed date in history is the execution date; a re-establishment threshold read from history uses it.

R7ASE SE-H (approved as declared boundaries E1-E6, with NF-R7ASE-2 recorded): the planner reads the planning view (E1); a run value read through an unreviewed week keeps that week’s evidence start and is not re-gated (E2, unchanged); completed sessions verify a sport only when the whole week executed it as assumed (E3, my S-A); a rebuilt value reads the evidence known at the cut (E4); weeks never reported are not history and the planner keeps its plan (E5, cost NF-R7ASE-1); a last-day handler applying the review’s rule is that sport’s review (E6).
